transcript.note: Round1: pure compaction pass, no vertex moves. The align result carried 8 empty columns and 10 empty rows (34x35 grid) that were never squeezed out during alignment; apply's compactGridSafe runs unconditionally even on a no-op move set, so this round just collapses those empty bands before any further H/V work.

Round2 (first real move round after the compaction-only pass). 37 (leaf, only neighbour 18) had been completely unaligned since round1 of the align chain reverted its attempted fix; moving it one column left lands it on a diagonal with 18. 55 (locked col25 via its other neighbour 32) moved up 2 rows to match 34's row (34 is its only other neighbour), turning the 34-55 gap into a horizontal while its vertical to 32 survives (column unchanged).

Round3. 13 (locked col19 via vertical to 6) dropped one row to land on 38's row, turning the 13-38 gap into a horizontal -- its vertical to 6 survives since only the row changed. 25 (locked col16 via vertical to 26) moved down 2 rows to match 39's row exactly, turning the 25-39 gap into a horizontal as well.

Round4. 9 (locked col18 via vertical to 10) moved down 2 rows to match 25's row exactly, upgrading their diagonal into a full horizontal while its vertical to 10 survives (column unchanged). The remaining off edges (45-36, 36-23, 23-20, 16-33, plus several diagonals) all sit between vertices that are individually and jointly at a local optimum -- every nearby candidate either re-creates the same alignment count or trades one aligned edge for another with no net gain, so this is where the loop converges.
